title: QBR - Aurora Systems Health Check
summary: Quarterly business review covering last quarter's consumption (tokens and embeddings), a notable cost spike in July tied to batch processing of support logs, latency SLAs, recent reliability incidents and mitigations, and roadmap alignment for upcoming dedicated capacity and Private deployment evaluation.
next_steps: Alex to send 90-day usage and cost breakdown by model (including per-route token counts) - due 2026-09-24
Diego to share preliminary Dedicated capacity options and estimated throughput for Aurora's peak QPS - due 2026-09-28
Priya to schedule security deep-dive (SOC 2 + network design) with Aurora's security team - proposed 2026-10-05
Maya to confirm pilot scope and propose 2-week evaluation prompts for model quality checks - due 2026-09-29
action_items: Alex Kim; Send 90-day usage & cost breakdown by model, per-route token counts; 2026-09-24
Diego Martinez; Provide Dedicated capacity pricing and throughput estimates for peak QPS; 2026-09-28
Priya Shah; Schedule SOC 2/network security deep-dive and share security pack; 2026-10-05
Maya Rodriguez; Share evaluation prompt set and success criteria for pilot; 2026-09-29
Sam Patel; Confirm budget window for Dedicated contract (Q4 commit or annual); 2026-10-02
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Kim: Hi everyone, thanks for joining the QBR, appreciate you taking the time. We'll run through usage, cost, reliability, and then roadmap. Priya and Diego from our side with me.
[00:12] Maya Rodriguez: Thanks Alex. We got the calendar invite, looking forward. Quick note Sam from finance is on for the cost bits.
[00:20] Priya Shah: Hey all, quick agenda - usage trends, recent incident recap, cost deep-dive, next steps for pilot / Dedicated evaluation.
[00:30] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. We had some internal spike questions, mostly July.
[00:35] Diego Martinez: I'll start with usage—over the last 90 days you've grown token consumption ~42% month-over-month in the support summarization pipeline. Most of the spike was embeddings+rerank for search.
[00:46] Maya: Right, July we ran a batch reindex that bumped things. I think part was KV cache misses because of long prefix variations, we weren't hitting cache effectively.
[00:58] Diego: Yeah, the pattern shows a lot of slightly different prompts which prevented prefix caching. Also a background job retried chunks which multiplied requests.
[01:10] Alex: On costs, Sam is the owner, but to call out the total hosted spend increased about 35% month over month in July, and unit cost per token went up because of the rerank jobs and some fallback to larger model when smaller model was returning lower quality.
[01:25] Sam Patel: Confirmed, that July number surprised finance. We need the per-model breakdown to show where to optimize.
[01:31] Priya: We'll send a per-route and per-model report. Diego — can you include the times of day for the big spikes so Aurora can consider windowing?
[01:39] Diego: Yep, will include 15-minute granularity for the peak days.
[01:44] [02:00] Liam: On latency, we've been seeing P95 climb during batch windows — target is 450ms P95; redwood's recent upgrade brought it from ~620ms to 480ms but still above goal.
[02:10] Diego: The P95 is sensitive to batching policy during peaks; default continuous batching favors throughput which increases tail lat. We recommended a small tweak to batching window and pre-warm cache for the support pipeline, that helped — we saw a drop to ~470ms after the tweak.
[02:26] Maya: So for production SLA, we'd likely want Dedicated capacity?
[02:30] Alex: That might be the right path. Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolations so you won't get noisy neighbor effects. We'll include Dedicated sizing options.
[02:38] Nora Li: We also want to evaluate Private deployment for data residency/security — some of these support logs are PII and legal wants controls.
[02:47] Priya: For Private we can do VPC + KMS integration; SOC 2 artifacts and audit logs are available. We'll bring security folks into a follow-up.
[02:56] [03:10] Maya: One reliability incident I want to cover: on 2026-07-23 we had a 90-minute outage for the embeddings route. What happened?
[03:18] Diego: That was a cascade from an autoscaler misconfiguration on your Dedicated test cluster — there was a bad readiness probe, pods were cycling and we hit capacity limits, fallback attempted to route to larger model which increased cost. We rolled back the autoscaler change and added better probe checks.
[03:33] Alex: We also added an automatic fallback policy that prefers same-family quantized variants before going to a larger dense model to reduce cost impact.
[03:42] Sam: Good — finance wants to understand how much that outage added to spend.
[03:47] Diego: I'll isolate the cost delta from the fallback routing and include it in the cost report.
[03:52] [04:05] Liam: For the pilot, we want to test Dedicated with a canary route for embeddings and keep the rest on hosted. Latency targets are 300ms P95 for the canary.
[04:15] Diego: That seems achievable with right VM sizing and pinned batches; we'll propose two capacity tiers — baseline and peak — and show expected P95 and cost.
[04:25] Maya: What about quantization? We tried int8 for a subset of models and saw quality regressions. Is there a recommended profile?
[04:34] Diego: We have per-model quantization profiles. For your rerank models, int8 gave small regressions; we recommend mixed-precision or 4-bit + eval on your prompt set before switching full time. Redwood Optimize can run the evals and give suggested profiles.
[04:50] [05:05] Priya: On roadmap — Aurora's ask was better token-level cost attribution and improved observability in the console for per-route KPIs. We have an upcoming console update in Q4 that adds token-level drilldowns and per-model SLO dashboards.
[05:20] Maya: That's great timing — helps our execs.
[05:24] Nora: Security — we need details on KMS integration and whether audit logs are immutable and exportable to our SIEM.
[05:33] Alex: Short answer: yes. We support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated, audit logs are exportable via syslog/S3, and we can set up log forwarding to your SIEM. We'll include the security pack and SOC 2 report.
[05:45] Priya: We'll also propose a joint session with our security engineer next Wednesday — is that feasible for Aurora?
[05:51] Nora: Yes, next Wed works for a 60-minute slot.
[05:56] [06:10] Maya: On commercial terms — if Dedicated looks good, what are typical commit windows? Q4 annual?
[06:18] Alex: We usually do monthly or annual reserved capacity. Annual gives better unit economics. We'll surface a pricing slide with two contract options — Q4 commit (shorter term) and annual reserved (discounted).
[06:29] Sam: Finance prefers to see the break-even on spend vs hosted in six months.
[06:34] Alex: We'll include a modeled cost comparison run-rate based on your 90-day usage.
[06:39] [06:50] Liam: Any blockers for the pilot? From infra side we need docs for VPC peering and private subnets, and confirmation on egress rules for KMS.
[06:58] Priya: We'll send the network design doc and KMS egress checklist.
[07:03] Diego: Also, we'll provide a small benchmark script you can run to validate latency from your region to our Dedicated endpoint before provisioning.
[07:12] Maya: Perfect.
[07:15] [07:30] Alex: To recap — action items: send 90-day usage & cost breakdown, Dedicated sizing and pricing, schedule security deep-dive, provide evaluation prompt set. Priya will coordinate next steps and Diego will lead technical follow-ups.
[07:44] Maya: Thanks, appreciate the thoroughness.
[07:48] Sam: Thanks everyone.
[07:50] Alex: We'll follow up with notes and a calendar for the security session.
[07:55] Priya: Thanks, everyone — end QBR.
